headline: High-risk shared-workspace coding pair: Cline can write/egress broadly while Great Expectations reads/writes data artifacts, creating default-path leakage and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read/write workspace files, run browsers, and use MCP; Great Expectations consumes and writes validation artifacts in files. That shared filesystem bridge makes prompt-like content in files plausible, though not proven as a default instruction channel. The interaction is pairwise and documented only indirectly, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory, file content can bridge them.
IF Great Expectations outputs are later parsed by Cline as instructions, injection risk materializes.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable Cline MCP servers for shared folders.
Require manual review of any file Cline reads from Great Expectations.
Prefix validation outputs with machine-only schemas.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline has broad network egress and handles model-provider API keys, while Great Expectations touches data sources, validation results, and documentation. If they share files, sensitive data can flow from Great Expectations into Cline’s browser/model context and then out over the network. The pairwise leakage path exists in default workspace-sharing setups.
conditions: IF the same data files are visible to both agents, Cline can ingest them.
IF Cline sends those contents to its configured model provider, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Use separate OS users or containers.
Exclude sensitive data directories from Cline workspace.
Turn off browser access for tasks involving secrets.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately after shared-workspace use.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent file ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline can write the filesystem, modify git state, and execute shell commands; Great Expectations can install packages and write validation artifacts. In a shared repo, both can mutate the same files and git state without any locking mechanism shown in either profile. That makes destructive overwrite or inconsistent repo state a default danger.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git checkout, concurrent writes can collide.
IF Great Expectations writes reports while Cline edits code, last-writer-wins corruption can occur.
mitigations: Assign one agent per repository checkout.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Commit or stash before switching agents.
Restrict Great Expectations to read-only validation runs.
requires-engineering: add file and git locks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code or browser-derived facts, and Great Expectations can consume those outputs as validation inputs. If Great Expectations treats Cline-produced artifacts as authoritative without a verification step, errors can cascade into incorrect tests or documentation. The pathway is plausible in default workflows, but not directly evidenced as automated action-taking.
conditions: IF Great Expectations ingests artifacts produced by Cline without independent checks, errors propagate.
IF Cline’s browser-derived claims are written into validation configs, downstream outputs can be wrong.
mitigations: Add a human review step before reuse of Cline outputs.
Validate schemas before Great Expectations consumes files.
Keep browser-derived notes separate from test inputs.
Require checksum or diff review for generated artifacts.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware gating.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either open-source profile. Cline handles model-provider API keys and broad network egress, while Great Expectations is local-file oriented with no egress; that suggests a possible policy mismatch only if sensitive data is routed through Cline’s external provider. I cite both because the compliance risk arises from their combined data flow.
conditions: IF regulated data is sent through Cline’s external model provider, residency or retention policy may be implicated.
IF Great Expectations processes the same regulated dataset locally, policy alignment must be checked.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Cline prompts.
Use a provider with an approved DPA.
Document retention settings for both tools.
Run Great Expectations on de-identified samples.
requires-engineering: add compliance routing controls.
